newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Saurer makes bid for BB.
newsitem.headline: Saurer makes bid for BB.

text.p: Textile machinery and components maker Saurer AG said it was launching a takeover offer to shareholders in Swiss investor BB Industrie Holding AG (BBI), which holds a 32 percent stake in Saurer.
"The board of directors of BBI recommends its shareholders accept the offer," a statement from Saurer said.
A BB spokesman confirmed that the holding company supported the takeover offer. "We agree with this," the spokesman told Reuters.
"Saurer plans to delist BBI on the bourse after the transaction," the Saurer statement said.
Saurer said it would offer three of its own registered shares plus 640 Swiss francs for each BBI bearer share.
BBI bearer shares closed before the takeover announcement at 2,765 Swiss francs, down five francs. Saurer registered shares closed eight francs higher at 745.
BBI was founded as an investment company to hold stakes in swiss and European industrial companies.
But Saurer shares and cash are its two main assets now since BBI sold a 35-percent stake in Swiss textile machiney and automotive supply group Rieter Holding AG in March.
A BBI spokesman declined to say how much cash the company had on hand.
BB Industrie said on April 9 it had expanded its stake in Saurer by 38,315 shares during the first quarter to total of 497,967 shares for a stake in Saurer of 32 percent.
"The offer is therefore four percent or 110 Swiss francs higher than today's closing price of 2,765," it said.
It said the complete, legally-binding offer would be made public at Saurer's annual results news conference on May 7.
"Saurer reserves the option of withdrawing from the offer is at least 70 percent of available BBI shares are not offered for takeover," the company said.

Saurer said it had already proposed paying out 15 Swiss francs of it own shares' nominal value. If approved by shareholders on May 28, this would bring BBI shareholders an additional payment of 45 Swiss francs per former BBI bearer.
